title: Assamese language
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
body:
Assamese is an Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in Assam, and the state's official language. It is written in the Assamese script, which is closely related to the Bengali script but has its own letters, including ৰ and ৱ.

Its literature goes back centuries, from the Vaishnavite writings of Srimanta Sankardev and Madhavdev to modern poetry, novels and songs. Assamese is also spoken in parts of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Bhutan.
extra:
Script and sounds

The Assamese script is an abugida: consonants carry an inherent vowel, changed by vowel signs. It is distinct from Bengali script in letters such as ৰ (ro) and ৱ (wo), and in its pronunciation.

Literature

Early Assamese literature includes the works of Sankardev and Madhavdev, the buranjis, and later the novels of Lakshminath Bezbarua and the songs of Jyoti Prasad Agarwala and Bhupen Hazarika.
